items.stem: What makes an AI-generated schema migration safe to run?

options.text: It is reversible, reviewed, and tested on a copy before production
options.rationale: Correct: reversibility, review and a tested dry run are the safeguards.

options.text: It ran once without an error message
options.rationale: Running without error does not prove data was preserved.

options.text: It was generated quickly by the agent
It drops the old table to keep things clean
options.rationale: A destructive drop with no rollback is the opposite of safe.

items.explanation: Correct: reversibility, review and a tested dry run are the safeguards.

items.stem: Which TWO practices confirm a refactor preserved the data? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Run a verification query comparing results before and after
options.rationale: Correct: comparing results proves the data is preserved.

options.text: Generate edge-case test rows and check the constraints hold
options.rationale: Correct: edge-case data exposes broken constraints.

options.text: Assume success because the migration script ran
options.rationale: Running is not evidence of correctness.

options.text: Delete the backup to save space
options.rationale: Removing the backup removes your recovery path.

items.explanation: Correct: comparing results proves the data is preserved.

items.stem: What should never be pasted into a Cursor prompt for a database task?

options.text: A production connection string or live credentials
options.rationale: Correct: credentials and connection strings must stay out of prompts.
A schema without secrets is appropriate context.

options.text: A plain-language description of the report needed
options.rationale: Requirements are safe and useful context.

options.text: A sample of synthetic test rows
options.rationale: Synthetic data carries no confidentiality risk.
